scope: Read-only reconstruction and review of the frozen seven-register architecture, its detailed role assignment, all register-to-register references, five frozen external support targets, and the support-level progression. This review creates new append-only review and contract artifacts only.

role_reviews.review: Responsibility is distinct from identity. Retain source, time window, listing scope, warnings, and non-atomicity as first-class observation context.

Use exact source-object instance as the candidate subject. Keep native source IDs and K501 IDs distinct. No hash/path/name-based identity collapse. Detailed issuance and equivalence rules must be pinned before this register schema is designed.
Artifact and artifact-version description is distinct from source-object identity. Explicitly reference exact object identities; never infer cardinality.
Separate requested and completed extent, read method, content/page/range coverage, warnings, and unread/deferral state. Never infer complete content coverage from metadata or snippets.
Every digest must be bound to exact bytes, algorithm, input identity, and scope. Integrity remains independent of DeepRead and semantics.
Retain one frozen register name but separate provenance records from rights records. Rights assertions require evidence and scope; technical access and provenance are not rights clearance.
Routes are versioned navigation declarations with time-scoped resolution observations. A route never creates identity, validates content, or authorizes access.

matrix_notes: NO_DIRECT_ARCHITECTURAL_REFERENCE means no mandatory direct record reference is defined in this contract; it does not prohibit a separately evidenced future relation.
References are authored by the row/source register and point to the column/target register. This direction is normative for the matrix.
Directory Register → Object Identity Register is optional and only allowed after identity is independently established.
Artifact Register → Object Identity Register records what object instance an artifact/version represents or contains.
DeepRead and Integrity each reference the exact source identity and/or artifact version they assess. They do not reference each other as a prerequisite.
Provenance and Rights may reference DeepRead and Integrity event records as supporting evidence, while the event records remain owned by their respective registers.
Route Registry may reference Directory, Object Identity, and Artifact targets. It never references a successful route as proof of access, rights, or semantic validity.

relationship_direction_corrections.review_finding: Direction conflicts with the accompanying statement that Artifact records reference Object Identity.
DeepRead event is the record that references the artifact/source revision it reads.
Integrity event is the record that references the exact artifact bytes/package payload it checks.

additional_reference_edges.reason: A read event must bind its coverage claim to the exact source-object instance when the native identity is available.
A digest/verification event must bind its byte-scope claim to the exact source-object instance when the native identity is available.
A provenance/preservation statement may cite an integrity event as supporting evidence; the Integrity Register remains the source of record for that event.

overlap_and_open_issue_register.decision: Directory stores observed location/time; Object Identity stores source-object identity. Directory may reference identity only when independently established.
Object Identity identifies a source-object instance. Artifact Register describes a representation/version and references source-object identities. One-to-many is allowed only when evidenced.
Artifact owns description/version; DeepRead owns read event and exact coverage. DeepRead references Artifact and Object Identity; Artifact does not own read status.
Artifact owns description/version; Integrity owns byte/digest evidence. Integrity references Artifact and Object Identity; no reciprocal ownership.
Reading content and verifying bytes are independent operations. Neither implies the other; both may reference the same source/artifact version.
Provenance may reference DeepRead/Integrity events when they support a derivation or preservation claim; those event records remain owned by their respective registers.

overlap_and_open_issue_register.topic: Provenance vs Rights within one frozen register
overlap_and_open_issue_register.decision: Keep one register, but distinguish PROVENANCE records from RIGHTS records. No legal permission is inferred from origin, technical access, or a license string alone.
Route stores locator and route resolution; target identity and artifact version are references only. Route resolution does not imply validity or permission.
Define deterministic assignment, source scope, duplicate/copy claims, revision relationship, and evidence required for equivalence before Object Identity schema design.

overlap_and_open_issue_register.topic: Artifact version and source-object relationship cardinality
overlap_and_open_issue_register.decision: Define version identity, immutable revision references, and relationship multiplicity in Artifact Register design; do not infer cardinality.
Define how correction, withdrawal, supersession, and status changes are appended without rewriting prior evidence.

overlap_and_open_issue_register.topic: Directory freshness and route temporal resolution
overlap_and_open_issue_register.decision: Define observation validity window, stale route handling, unresolved/expired states, and source-interface time semantics.
Define evidence scope, applicable rights/permission statement, reviewer authority, decision time, restrictions, and UNKNOWN/OPEN states. No default legal conclusion.
Define requested vs completed extents, extraction methods, coverage states, and how partial/failed reads are represented without false completion.

overlap_and_open_issue_register.topic: Integrity algorithm and verification event semantics
overlap_and_open_issue_register.decision: Define supported algorithms, byte scope, canonical byte acquisition, verifier provenance, and result state per exact verification event.
Define explicit values for unmapped, unsupported, omitted, normalized, defaulted, and lossy fields before any crosswalk or adapter is accepted.
No support or compatibility is inferred from the frozen RO-Crate 1.2 target.

standard_reviews.name: JSON Schema
standard_reviews.decision_detail: Applies to the structure and allowed value constraints of machine-readable records for all seven registers, Gateway documents, support profiles, and adapter documents. It is structural validation only.
standard_reviews.required_clarification: JSON Schema does not establish that referenced IDs exist or that cross-register graph relationships are valid. Referential/graph checking remains a separate validator work unit.
standard_reviews.external_boundary: No source truth, identity authority, DeepRead completeness, rights clearance, or canonicality is proved by schema validation.

standard_reviews.name: W3C PROV-O
standard_reviews.decision_detail: PROV-O Entity/Activity/Agent concepts can represent source/derived entities, read or transformation activities, and responsible agents. K501 identities remain authoritative references; artifact versions and DeepRead events retain their native records.
standard_reviews.required_clarification: Add Object Identity Register to the related-register mapping. Keep rights decisions outside PROV-O semantics; provenance vocabulary is not a rights-clearance authority. DeepRead coverage detail remains owned by DeepRead Register.
standard_reviews.external_boundary: The PROV-O graph is a derived representation and cannot redefine K501 object identity, source scope, temporal rules, or status values.

standard_reviews.name: PREMIS Data Dictionary
standard_reviews.decision_detail: PREMIS Object/Event/Agent/Rights entities provide bounded preservation metadata mappings. Artifact and integrity records provide preservation object/fixity information; Provenance and Rights provides rights and responsible-agent evidence.
standard_reviews.required_clarification: Add Object Identity Register as the K501 identity reference for PREMIS Objects. The relation is not assumed to be one-to-one. DeepRead events map only when they qualify as declared preservation events; not every read is automatically a PREMIS event.
standard_reviews.external_boundary: PREMIS Object identifiers and semantic units do not replace K501 identity or artifact-version definitions. Rights statements in PREMIS do not create legal authority absent source evidence.

standard_reviews.name: The BagIt File Packaging Format
standard_reviews.decision_detail: Directory observations provide source locators/hierarchy candidates for package payload layout; Artifact Register describes the BagIt package as an artifact; Integrity Register records package-scoped payload and tag fixity checks.
standard_reviews.required_clarification: Add Directory Register to the related-register mapping. Provenance/Rights may supply optional bag metadata, but BagIt is not a provenance ontology or rights-clearance mechanism. Any K501 object identifier carried as metadata remains a K501 value, not a BagIt identity.
standard_reviews.external_boundary: A complete/valid BagIt claim is limited to the exact bag and files enumerated and checked under RFC 8493. It does not imply Library-wide coverage, semantic correctness, rights, or canonicality.

standard_reviews.name: RO-Crate
standard_reviews.decision_detail: RO-Crate 1.2 JSON-LD can describe a Root Data Entity, data entities, and contextual entities. It is suitable for selected K501 package/artifact descriptions and context. Directory structure can inform package hierarchy; K501 source IDs may be preserved as external identifiers where appropriate.
standard_reviews.required_clarification: Add Directory Register as a source of package/file-structure observations. Remove Route Registry from direct mapped registers: RO-Crate file URLs/identifiers are not equivalent to K501 route declarations or route-resolution evidence. Preserve Object Identity only as K501 identifier references, not as a replaced RO-Crate identity.
standard_reviews.external_boundary: RO-Crate 1.2 does not require every file to appear as a Data Entity. It is not a complete Library inventory, file-level identity register, DeepRead record, or K501 route registry. RO-Crate 1.3 remains a separate compatibility review.

support_level_model_review.evaluation_unit: Each result is scoped to exact standard/version + adapter version + operation direction + input/output identity + test fixture/scope. No global standard-level PASS is inferred.

progression.meaning: The exact standard/version and bounded K501 integration purpose are recorded in an accepted, versioned support profile.
progression.limit: A draft or target selection alone is not an accepted registration; this level does not imply a parser or implementation.

progression.meaning: A concrete input document/package is read by an identified parser within the pinned version and scope.
evidence: Exact input identity and byte/scope reference.
Parse result, warnings, and unsupported constructs.
progression.limit: Parsing alone does not establish validation or correctness.

progression.meaning: The parsed input passes the declared syntax/schema/profile checks for the pinned version and profile.
evidence: Validation report, scope, warnings, and result.
progression.limit: Validation is not proof of truth, completeness, rights, identity, or canonicality.

progression.meaning: A versioned K501-to-standard or standard-to-K501 mapping is defined and applied to a declared scope.
evidence: Explicit unmapped, unsupported, defaulted, transformed, and lossy elements.
progression.limit: Mapping does not change K501 native semantics.

progression.meaning: A concrete export or import is performed through a declared adapter boundary. The direction is recorded explicitly; both outcomes may exist for a bidirectional adapter.
evidence: Adapter/version, time, transformation evidence, and losses.
progression.limit: A one-way export or import is not round-trip verification; ROUNDTRIP_VERIFIED requires both directions and a scoped comparison.

progression.meaning: A bidirectional export/import cycle passes declared tests for the exact fixture, fields, and invariants.
evidence: Fixture, expected invariant set, and comparison method.
Observed results, losses, warnings, and report.
progression.limit: Applies only to the tested scope; not universal semantic equivalence or full-system conformance.

support_level_model_review.flow_rule: REGISTERED -> PARSED -> VALIDATED -> MAPPED -> (EXPORTED or IMPORTED); ROUNDTRIP_VERIFIED requires both directions and a scoped comparison. EXPORTED and IMPORTED are distinct directional outcomes, not synonyms.
support_level_model_review.current_achieved_levels: NOT_ASSERTED; profile detail remains a draft until separately accepted.
